profile.reading:
This combined row carries two CyrusOne site codes, SAT10 and SAT11, which this registry's prior research found correspond to two genuinely distinct street addresses (14785 Omicron Drive and 15355 Lambda Drive respectively per aggregator listings) rather than one shared campus address; which specific building this row's mapped coordinates (reverse-geocoded to Zeta Drive, Bexar County, TX 78253) represent was not resolved, so neither individual address is asserted here as confirmed for this row, and no technical_space_sqft or it_capacity_mw figure is asserted.

CyrusOne's first San Antonio facility opened in 2012; per CyrusOne's own press release on its fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6, broken ground January 2025 in Texas Research Park), the company had invested approximately $1 billion in capital to date across its San Antonio campuses as of that release, and describes SAT5-SAT6 itself as two buildings totaling 276,000 sq ft and 36 MW of IT capacity, figures that differ somewhat from an earlier operator-page-sourced figure of 175,000 sq ft/33 MW recorded for that campus elsewhere in this registry, a discrepancy noted rather than silently reconciled. The San Antonio Report, a local nonprofit newsroom, reported in 2026 that the city hosts more than 20 operational data centers with 59 more in various planning stages; CPS Energy, the municipally owned utility, supplies power to 21 of the existing facilities (generating roughly $110 million in revenue) and has projected future data center energy demand in the metro at approximately 26,000 megawatts, while flagging water use as a growing constraint: data centers currently draw about 0.1% of San Antonio Water System's drinking water, but planned new facilities have requested roughly 600 acre-feet of drinking water and 3,000 acre-feet of recycled water against a system that has capacity for only about 10,000 additional acre-feet before requiring upgrades.

reading.body:
CyrusOne SAT10 and SAT11 are two distinct buildings in San Antonio whose individual addresses and capacities are not published by the operator. This registry maps them as a combined entity at coordinates that reverse-geocode to Zeta Drive, but cannot confirm which building those coordinates represent or resolve the published IT capacity for either facility. The specific power draw and rack density of this campus therefore remain unknown.

San Antonio hosts more than 20 operational data centers today with 59 more in planning stages, according to local reporting from 2026. CyrusOne has invested approximately $1 billion across its San Antonio campuses since 2012. The municipal utility CPS Energy supplies power to 21 existing facilities and projects data center demand in the metro to reach roughly 26,000 megawatts, though water availability is becoming a constraint, with planned facilities requesting 3,600 acre-feet of combined drinking and recycled water against a system capacity of only 10,000 additional acre-feet.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish power figures totaling 468 megawatts. This campus, without a published capacity figure, cannot be ranked within the state's published capacity total. Whether SAT10 and SAT11 are material to AI scaling cannot be determined from available operator disclosures.
